narrative:
FRIDAY MAY 29, PRE-OPEN — RELIEF RALLY DAY 3, STAY CONSTRUCTIVE BUT DISCIPLINED.

WHAT JUST HAPPENED (May 28 reopen)
- KSE-100 closed 171,725 (+2.31% / +3,881 pts) — broad, strong.
- Cement led: MLCF +5.95, KOHC +5.79, FCCL +5.53, DGKC +5.28.
- Banks strong: NBP +4.99, HBL +4.52, BAHL +4.25, UBL +2.34.
- E&P core +1.6% (OGDC +2.0, PPL +2.3, MARI +2.3); ATRL +1.0.

WHY (root cause)
- Brent has collapsed from ~USD 110 (May 19 panic) to USD 92. The
  oil-spike fear that caused the May 18 -3,791pt crash has fully
  reversed. That is import-bill relief for the macro AND input-cost
  relief for cement/power — hence cement's +5 macro tilt and the lead.
- US-Iran 60-day truce renewal underpins the risk-on tone.
- SBP foreign non-resident shareholding reform lowers FII friction
  for banks specifically.

WHAT'S DIFFERENT THIS TIME (the fix)
- The new relief-rally override is LIVE: the de-risk regime is now
  OFF (it was wrongly ON through May 19-25, when it force-downgraded
  8 banks/cement names to AVOID that then rallied >8%). Today's
  rule-based batch produced ZERO forced AVOIDs — banks (BAHL, NBP) and
  cement (DGKC) are HOLD, not AVOID. That is the gap closing.
- The short kill-switch flags cement (DGKC/KOHC, both +5%+ and well
  above 5-day highs) as squeeze-extended — do NOT short them.

THE CATCH
- This is still a LOCAL bid: foreign net-selling is now 5 days running
  (cum -2.94 PKR mn). Local-only relief rallies can fade fast if
  foreign doesn't follow, and the truce is one headline away from
  reversing the whole oil trade. So: participate in quality, do NOT
  chase what already ran, keep real cash.

TODAY'S PRIORITIES (May 29)
1. HOLD E&P core (OGDC, PPL, POL, MARI) — highest-quality longs;
   oil stabilized ~USD 92 + truce. ADD only on a pullback, don't chase.
2. SCALE banks (MCB, UBL, MEBL) on the SBP reform — but the names
   already +4-5% (NBP, HBL, BAHL) are NOT chase candidates today.
3. CEMENT: HOLD if owned (macro +5 tailwind), but do NOT initiate
   fresh after a +5-6% day. No shorts (kill-switch active).
4. CASH 40% (down from 45%) — macro improved (oil down, truce holding),
   but keep dry powder for the fragile-truce oil-spike risk.
5. AVOID unchanged: KEL/HUBC/KAPCO/NPL/EPCL — circular-debt/leverage
   names; their bounce is technical, not structural.
